# OpenForecast

> The unified interface for forecasting. Point-in-time forecasting is first-class: real
> historical forecast vintages are trained on directly, and an artifact
> records whether its origins were observed or simulated.

One name per intent — `fit`, `forecast`, `backtest`, `eligible_models` — over
any provider, any transport and both semantic data sources. Every page below
is served as Markdown at the address shown, and every Python example on one is
executed by the test suite.

## Overview

- [Home](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/index.md): The unified interface for forecasting.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/getting-started/installation.md): OpenForecast needs Python 3.11 or newer.
- [Quickstart](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/getting-started/quickstart.md): The whole workflow, on one page, against the model every install ships with.
- [Concepts in five minutes](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/getting-started/concepts.md): Five ideas carry the whole library.
- [Executable examples](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/getting-started/examples.md): Seven scripts live in [`examples/`](https://github.com/Garsdal/openforecast/tree/main/examples) in the repository.

## Guides

- [Event-time data](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/event-time.md): `TimeSeriesFrame` is ordinary `instance × event_time × variable` data: what happened, once per event time.
- [Point-in-time data](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/point-in-time.md): A `ForecastDataset` is what production pipelines already emit: every forecast vintage as it was issued, paired with the outcome it was trying to predict.
- [Fitting](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/fitting.md): A fit takes what to fit, the data, and — when the model needs more than the defaults — how to fit it.
- [Forecasting](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/forecasting.md): Three things are the same argument: the handle a fit returned, a pinned revision, and the alias that follows the latest one.
- [Backtesting](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/backtesting.md): The same models, over the same origins, scored the same way — and it is a loop over `fit` and `forecast` rather than any provider's backtester.
- [Probabilistic forecasts](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/probabilistic.md): What kind of answer to produce is a request; what a model can answer is a declaration.
- [Pipelines and ensembles](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/ensembles.md): Three things stay separate: what to fit, how to fit it, and what to predict.
- [The command line](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/guides/cli.md): Everything OpenForecast does is reachable from a shell, and the CLI is deliberately uncreative: a group and a verb at most, `--json` on everything that produces information, stdout for the answer and stderr for everything else.

## For agents

- [Overview](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/agents/overview.md): This section is for a reader that arrives with a fetch tool and a task, not with an afternoon.
- [Choosing a model](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/agents/choosing-a-model.md): Do not try models until one works.
- [Point-in-time rules](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/agents/point-in-time.md): This is the one part of the library where a request that looks right can be wrong, so it is stated as rules.
- [The structured CLI](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/agents/structured-cli.md): No Python signature to reverse-engineer, no doc page to trust, and no schema pinned to a version other than the one installed.
- [Recovering from errors](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/agents/errors.md): Every failure, at every boundary, carries the same three fields.

## Concepts

- [The data model](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/concepts/data-model.md): `TimeSeriesFrame` holds `instance × event_time × variable`: what happened.
- [Point-in-time semantics](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/concepts/point-in-time.md): Nothing deduplicates on event time, forward-fills across origins, or replaces an early vintage with a later revision.
- [Execution views](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/concepts/execution-views.md): A provider never sees a semantic dataset.
- [Model lifecycles](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/concepts/model-lifecycle.md): Whether anything has been fitted is a question for the registry, not for the string.
- [Providers](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/concepts/providers.md): Nixtla wants one version of `torch`, Darts wants another, sktime wants scikit-learn and statsmodels, the Chronos integration wants `torch` and `transformers`, and OpenForecast wants none of it.

## Integrations

- [Nixtla](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/integrations/nixtla.md): `integrations/nixtla`, published as `openforecast-nixtla`, wrapping `statsforecast` and `neuralforecast`.
- [Darts](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/integrations/darts.md): `integrations/darts`, published as `openforecast-darts`.
- [sktime](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/integrations/sktime.md): `integrations/sktime`, published as `openforecast-sktime`.
- [scikit-learn](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/integrations/sklearn.md): `integrations/sklearn`, published as `openforecast-sklearn`.
- [Chronos](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/integrations/chronos.md): `integrations/chronos`, published as `openforecast-chronos`, providing the `amazon` namespace.

## Reference

- [Overview](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/index.md): OpenForecast 0.1.0. `openforecast.__all__` is the whole public surface of the library and is asserted exactly, so this table is that assertion rendered: a name that is not here is not public.
- [Client and operations](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/client.md): The four operations, and the client every one of them is a method on.
- [Semantic data](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/data.md): What you hand OpenForecast: ordinary event-time data, real forecast vintages, and one inference origin cut out of them.
- [Models and descriptors](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/models.md): A model reference, and what one resolves to.
- [Recipes](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/recipes.md): What to fit: models, pipelines, ensembles, reductions and transforms.
- [Plans, tasks and outputs](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/tasks.md): How to fit it, what to predict, and what kind of answer to produce.
- [Forecasts](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/forecasts.md): What a forecast is: one long table, and the projections of it.
- [Backtesting and metrics](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/evaluation.md): Comparing models over origins, and scoring what comes back.
- [Transports](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/transports.md): Where a client executes, which is the only thing a transport decides.
- [Errors](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/reference/generated/errors.md): Every failure OpenForecast raises deliberately, with the `error.code` a caller branches on instead of on the prose.

## Optional

- [Everything above, in one file](https://garsdal.github.io/openforecast/llms-full.txt): the whole corpus concatenated, for a single fetch.
- [Repository](https://github.com/Garsdal/openforecast): the library, the integrations, the executable examples under `examples/`, and the seven architecture rules.
- [OpenAPI document](https://github.com/Garsdal/openforecast/blob/main/spec/openapi/openapi.json): the HTTP projection, generated from the request models.
- [JSON Schemas](https://github.com/Garsdal/openforecast/tree/main/spec/schemas): what each request has to look like, generated from the models that validate it.
